Contract Type Matrix

Compare contract structures by need pattern, supplier model, ordering logic, duration, competition and execution. Procedure thresholds remain a separate decision.

1FIXED NEED

One-off Contract

For a clearly defined, quantifiable need that is unlikely to recur.

  • Single supplier
  • Defined quantity / deliverables
  • No renewal
  • Concrete delivery deadline
∞RECURRING

Framework Contract

For recurring needs that can be defined as units while total volume remains uncertain.

  • One or several suppliers
  • Order forms
  • Ranking or pooling
  • Unit prices fixed
↻VARIABLE / COMPLEX

Framework Agreement

For regular but variable, uncertain or complex needs requiring mini-competition.

  • Multiple suppliers
  • Call-offs
  • Mini-competition per need
  • Adaptable specifications
One-off Contract
FIXED NEED

Best when deliverables and quantity are clearly defined and the need is unlikely to recur.

SUPPLIER MODELOne supplier; lots may be awarded separately.
ORDERING / COMPETITIONDirect contract; no additional competition after signature.
DURATIONRuns until obligations are completed; cannot be renewed.
KEY CONTROLAvoid repeated one-off contracts for the same foreseeable structural need.
Framework Contract
RECURRING

Best when the need recurs, units can be defined, but total volume remains uncertain.

SUPPLIER MODELSimple (one supplier) or multiple (several suppliers).
ORDERINGOrder forms; multiple FC uses ranking or pooling fixed before launch.
DURATIONGenerally max 4 years; 5 only exceptionally.
KEY CONTROLMonitor cumulative expenditure and keep orders inside FC scope/items.
Framework Agreement
VARIABLE / COMPLEX

Best for regular but variable, uncertain or complex needs where precise deliverables are not known upfront.

SUPPLIER MODELMultiple suppliers; guide recommends at least three per lot/agreement.
ORDERING / COMPETITIONCall-off mini-competition among preselected suppliers for each need.
DURATIONGenerally max 4 years; 5 only exceptionally.
KEY CONTROLCall-offs stay inside FA scope; ≥ €184k routes to Tenders Board.

Contract ≠ procedure

One-off, FC and FA describe the legal/operational structure. Direct award, competitive bidding and international public call describe the procedure used to award it.

Framework Contract

Use when the unit is known and the need repeats. For intellectual services, pooling is generally more flexible than ranking under the applicable rules.

Framework Agreement

Use when the need itself is variable and suppliers must compete again through call-offs. The guide describes FAs as administratively heavier.

€184K OVERRIDEThe Procurement Guide still contains the former €171,000 references. This tool applies the user-provided updated international threshold of €184,000 to threshold-dependent routing.

Calculate the total need, not each invoice

Include the full intended duration, renewals, lots, options and the expected cumulative order forms/call-offs. Thresholds are calculated per need, not per supplier or year.

Extrabudgetary / mixed funding

For €55,000–€184,000, competitive bidding and exceptional direct-award routes require a Legal Compliance Review before CCM approval. This control also applies where extrabudgetary funding is only partial.

Near €184,000?

If there is even a slight risk of reaching the international tender threshold, the Procurement Guide recommends launching an international public call for tenders from the outset.

SPECIAL ROUTEA sector-based approach for transversal needs across several co-operation projects requires an international public call for tenders. Framework-agreement call-offs above €184,000 are subject to the Tenders Board.

Document Clarification Gate

A fast decision aid for incomplete or unclear bids. The guide distinguishes omissions that are fundamental to the bid from non-essential information/documents that may be requested through clarification.

×

Fundamental to the bid

If the omission or lack of clarity is fundamental, clarification should not be used to repair or materially change the submitted offer.

  • Incomplete or unclear bids are in principle inadmissible.
  • Clarification must not change the principal features of the bid.
  • If a significant change would be needed, this is no longer a simple clarification.
✓

Non-essential information / documents

Where the omission or lack of clarity is not fundamental, the buyer entity may request clarification or missing non-essential information/documents.

  • Request must be made in writing.
  • Keep all exchanges on record.
  • Inform the CCM or Tenders Board when presenting results for validation.
  • Consult DLAPIL in case of doubt.
Incomplete / unclear bid→Is the missing point fundamental?→YES: do not cure through clarificationorNO: written clarification may be possible

    Operational notes

    1. Once the AWP is approved, the reference allows limited flexibility above the activity budget without full re-approval.
    2. Material increases to a PO amount should be routed for prior CCM approval in line with the applicable authorisation rules.
    3. Contracts with substantive elements such as consultants and grants require Content Manager validation, or the relevant superior where applicable.
    4. The AWP should cover the relevant implementation period and be reviewed periodically.
    5. Contracts under decentralised management must follow the applicable CCM signature route.
    6. For the current tool, procurements in the €55k–€184k band should follow the applicable legal/procurement review route; this reflects the updated threshold used elsewhere in this guide.

      PROJECT FINANCE · 2026 CLOSING

      End of Year Procedure

      A simple project-team checklist for closing 2026: check delivery dates, complete payment files, follow up suppliers and finalise POs when the expenditure is fully recorded.

      2026 Financial Year Closing
      2026 · THREE RULES TO REMEMBER
      📅 Delivery by 31/12/2026

      Only goods delivered and services rendered by 31 December 2026 can be included in 2026 expenditure.

      💼 Both budget types

      The year-end accounting rules apply to annual budgets and special accounts.

      ✅ Check before finalising

      Finalise a 2026 PO only when all expenditure has been recorded in FIMS. Check “Amount billed” / “Invoices” on the Fiche PO. You do not need to wait for payment.

      🔔
      Start early — do not wait for the final closing deadline.
      Review open POs, ask suppliers for missing invoices and send complete payment files to Finance as soon as they are ready.

      2026 Closing Ribbon

      Select a phase to see the action, owner, control point and evidence to keep.

      1
      NOW

        🧾 Complete filesSend payment files to Finance as soon as the invoice and supporting documents are ready.
        🔎 Check Fiche POBefore finalising, confirm that all expenditure appears under Amount billed / Invoices.
        📦 Check delivery dateFor 2026 expenditure, the goods or service must relate to delivery/performance by 31 December 2026.

        Which Financial Year?

        Use the 2026 expenditure-allocation table to identify the expected treatment. This is a guide for the closing check, not a replacement for Finance validation.

        2026 → 2027

        ✓ Project team — Do

        • Check open POs regularly.
        • Follow up suppliers for missing invoices and documents.
        • Send completed payment files to Finance without waiting for the last day.
        • Finalise POs as soon as possible once all expenditure is recorded.

        ⚠ Avoid

        • Finalising a PO before checking Amount billed / Invoices in the Fiche PO.
        • Including 2027 delivery as 2026 expenditure.
        • Waiting for the supplier payment before finalising an otherwise complete PO.
        • Leaving missing invoices or blocked files until the final deadline.

        ›Petty Cash
        PROJECT FINANCE · QUICK CONTROL

        Petty Cash Limits

        Use petty cash only for small-value operational needs, within the authorised limit, with a clear supporting file.

        Projects

        €100

        Maximum petty cash limit for project-related expenses.

        Ordinary Budget (OB)

        €50

        Maximum petty cash limit for OB-related expenses.

        ⚠ Petty cash should remain an exception route for small-value operational needs. Avoid split transactions or repeated use for expenses that should follow the normal PO/payment workflow.
        🛡️

        CCM approval is required before spending

        Do not make the purchase first and seek approval afterwards. Confirm the CCM approval before any petty cash expense is incurred.

        PRE-SPEND CONTROL

        Appropriate use

        • Small-value operational need
        • Within the applicable limit
        • CCM approval obtained before the expense
        • Clear purpose and coding
        • Readable receipt or invoice kept in the file

        Do not use for

        • Split or repeated purchases
        • Items that should follow the normal procurement route
        • Unsupported or personal expenses
        • Costs above the authorised petty cash limit
        • Any expense made before CCM approval

        Good filing habit: keep editable working files and final signed PDFs together in the correct DMS location, and use consistent names so another colleague can understand the file without reconstructing the history.
        Editable + SignedKeep final PDF evidence together with the relevant editable source where applicable.
        TraceableStore approvals, clarifications and correspondence with the related transaction.
        Consistent namingUse clear names, dates and references so files remain searchable.
